questions.q: Why does the storefront API use azurerm_linux_web_app instead of azurerm_linux_virtual_machine?
options: App Service does not support Linux
The API is a standard web application with no need to manage an operating system -- App Service handles the runtime
azurerm_linux_web_app is deprecated and should be avoided
Web apps cannot be connected to a storage account
questions.explain: App Service is a platform-as-a-service offering; it runs the application code without requiring the team to patch or manage an underlying VM.

questions.q: What does container_access_type = "blob" on azurerm_storage_container configure?
options: It encrypts every blob in the container at rest
It allows anonymous public read access to individual blobs in the container
It restricts the container to a single virtual network
It sets the maximum file size allowed in the container
questions.explain: container_access_type = "blob" permits anonymous read access to individual blobs -- appropriate for public assets like product images, not for sensitive data.

questions.q: Where should the database connection string's actual value be written, according to this lesson's Key Vault example?
options: Hardcoded directly as a string in the resource block
Committed to version control in a separate secrets.tf file
Supplied via a variable such as var.db_connection_string at apply time, never typed into the configuration file
Stored as a comment above the resource block
questions.explain: The guide shows value = var.db_connection_string specifically so the real secret is supplied at apply time and never appears in the .tf source.

questions.q: What is the purpose of azurerm_key_vault_access_policy in this lesson's example?
options: It deletes the secret after a set time period
It grants the storefront web app's managed identity permission to read (Get) the one secret it needs
It encrypts the entire Key Vault with a customer-managed key
It creates a backup copy of the Key Vault in another region
questions.explain: The access policy grants secret_permissions = ["Get"] to the web app's managed identity, following least-privilege: read access to one secret, nothing more.

questions.q: Why does the storage account for product images use account_replication_type = "GRS" rather than LRS?
options: GRS is required for all Azure storage accounts by default
GRS is cheaper than LRS
GRS geo-replicates the data to a paired region, which is reasonable for customer-facing images that should survive a regional outage
LRS does not support blob containers
questions.explain: GRS (geo-redundant storage) replicates data to a paired Azure region, offering resilience against a regional failure, unlike LRS which only keeps copies in one datacenter.
